newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian advisory body opposes oil price rises.
newsitem.headline: Indian advisory body opposes oil price rises.

text.p: India's ruling centre-left coalition's decision-making Steering Committee has asked Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government not to raise the price of petroleum products, local news agencies said on Friday.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan as saying the Steering Committee asked the government at a three-hour meeting on Thursday to explore other means of curbing the burgeoning cost of oil subsidies.
The communist parties, which are key members of Deve Gowda's coalition, opposed an increase in petroleum prices, saying it would spur inflation.

Petroleum Ministry officials have said the prices must be hiked to bridge a rising deficit in the oil pool account, which is the amount the government owes India's oil firms for selling petroleum products to consumers below world prices.
The Petroleum Ministry has estimated the deficit will reach 155 billion rupees by the end of the 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal year.
PTI quoted Finance Minister P. Chidambaram as saying the deficit was rising and could reach 170 billion rupees by the end of March.
Deve Gowda said earlier this week that the government had to resort to borrowing to plug the deficit on the oil pool account.
But the Steering Commitee felt that government borrowing to plug the deficit was only a temporary measure, the PTI reported.
United News of India quoted Chidambaram as saying that inflation would be pushed up even if the government refrained from raising prices and met the oil pool shortfall through deficit financing.
